title: Microsoft Copilot Studio: workflow agent node can return generated files
summary: Hold: the briefing says exhausting prepaid capacity blocks new workflow runs, but Microsoft now says runs are blocked when the environment has no credits available, including its overage sources. The allocation API is documented despite the automatic warning; the control paths and conflicting workflow licensing guidance need minor clarifications.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing: Caps; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A published environment-group rule governing tenant-pool draw makes the environment-level setting read-only.
claims.quote: When you publish a rule, it governs every environment in the group. The environment-level setting becomes read-only in the Power Platform admin center, and programmatic requests can't override it.

claims.claim: Programmatic attempts to override a published tenant-pool group rule are rejected with TenantPoolLockedByPolicy.
claims.quote: Updates through the Power Platform admin center, Power Platform API, or administration SDKs are rejected with the TenantPoolLockedByPolicy error.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Caps; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Administrators can change and republish the environment-group rule to change its governed tenant-pool setting.
claims.quote: Change and republish the rule for the environment group, or remove the environment from the group to manage the setting independently.

claims.claim: Removing the environment from the group allows its tenant-pool setting to be managed independently.
claims.quote: After removal, the environment retains the value last applied by the group, but the setting becomes editable.

claims.claim: Clearing tenant-pool draw does not prevent usage being billed through a linked pay-as-you-go plan.
claims.quote: If the environment is linked to a pay-as-you-go billing plan, usage can continue through the linked Azure subscription.
